sections.markdown:
## C — School bus and motorcycle endorsements, renewal and expiration rules, donor choices, reasons a license is lost, and the three GDL steps
Knowledge domain: the endorsements a non-commercial Missouri license can carry, how and when to renew, what happens when a license lapses, the donor question at the counter, the conduct that costs a license, and the permit, intermediate and full under-twenty-one steps of the Graduated Driver License (GDL) law.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
A school bus (S) endorsement is needed to carry students between home, school and school-sponsored events in any vehicle built for more than ten passengers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Only drivers who are at least 21 and already carry either a Class E for-hire license or a commercial license bearing the Passenger (P) endorsement can receive the school bus endorsement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Failing a drug, alcohol or chemical test given under school bus law can suspend the school bus endorsement for one year. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
A school bus endorsement holder aged 75 or older must pass school bus skills testing every two years to keep it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Adding the motorcycle (M) endorsement to an existing license takes the motorcycle written test, vision and road sign tests, and a skills test on a motorcycle or motortricycle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
The Department mails a renewal reminder to the mailing address on your record, but none is sent for a temporary instruction permit or a commercial learner's permit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
You may renew up to six months before the license expires, and every renewal includes the vision and road sign tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
Renewing on time is your own duty even if no reminder arrives, and driving on a lapsed license can earn a ticket for driving without a valid license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
If you will be away from the state or country for a long period, a license office can grant an early renewal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
A Missouri driver license can be valid for as long as six years, and once it expires you may not drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
Missing the renewal by more than six months (184 days) after expiration means retaking the written and driving tests on top of the vision and road sign tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
Service members whose license expired while out of state can renew without re-examination for up to six months after an honorable discharge or within 90 days of moving back, whichever comes first, but the expired license still cannot be used to drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
A lost, stolen or destroyed license is replaced with a duplicate, though if it expires within six months you can renew early instead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A non-commercial driver can renew, after the vision and road sign tests, while suspended; during a revocation, renewal is allowed only if the revocation came from refusing a chemical test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A renewed license is not handed back until the reinstatement requirements are met and the driving privilege is restored. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
Answering yes to the donor question at the counter adds you to the Missouri Organ and Tissue Donor Registry, a first-person consent registry whose decision stands unless you change it and needs no family consent. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
Choosing the optional donor symbol puts a red heart with a green banner on the front of your permit, license or nondriver ID, and neither the symbol nor registry enrollment costs anything. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A03
A deaf or hard of hearing applicant may ask for a DHH notation, which must be requested when applying, so emergency and police personnel can quickly recognize the need. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A05
A parent or guardian of an applicant under 18 can file Form 4811 asking the Director of Revenue to deny a license, which also cancels a license already held; the denial lasts until age 18 or until the parent asks to clear it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A05
A license can be suspended, revoked or denied for driving under the influence, refusing an alcohol or drug test, leaving a crash scene, not filing an accident report, or lying on a license application. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A06
A license can also be lost for not keeping insurance, too many points, lending your license, skipping court or unpaid tickets, unpaid child support, skipping a required ignition interlock, stealing fuel, a minor possessing liquor, or failing to yield and causing injury or death. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A06
Altering your license or using someone else's to buy alcohol, ignoring a Driver License Bureau exam request, using a vehicle in a felony or causing a death in a crash, and submitting false proof of insurance are further grounds for losing a license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A06
Missouri's GDL law makes every first-time driver under 18 hold an instruction permit and drive with a licensed driver, then drive under restrictions on an intermediate license, before a full license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A06
GDL step one, the instruction permit at age 15, requires passing the vision, road sign and written tests and is valid up to 12 months depending on document verification. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A06
A parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer from a federal residential job training program must come to the license office to sign the permit permission statement. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A06
Under 16, a permit holder may drive only with a front-seat companion who is a parent, stepparent, grandparent, legal guardian or qualified instructor, or someone at least 25 who has been licensed at least three years and has written parent permission. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A06
From age 16 a permit holder may drive with a front-seat companion who is at least 21 and holds a valid license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A06
Permit drivers and all passengers must wear seat belts, the permit itself must be carried because the exam record is not enough, and the permit can be renewed repeatedly without new written tests. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A07
To move to the intermediate license you must hold the permit for at least six months (182 days), counted from the day after it was issued. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A07
The permit period must include 40 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction, at least ten of them after dark, given by a parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A07
GDL step two, the intermediate license for ages 16 to 18, requires no alcohol-related convictions in the past 12 months and no traffic convictions in the past six months. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A07
An adult from the approved list must come to the license office to confirm the 40 hours, and the applicant must pass the driving test and retake the vision, road sign and written tests if earlier results are more than one year old. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A07
In the first six months an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger under 19 who is not immediate family. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A07
After the first six months the limit becomes no more than three passengers under 19 who are not immediate family. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A07
An intermediate driver may not drive alone from 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. unless going to or from a school activity, job or emergency, or riding with a licensed driver 21 or older. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A07
For the passenger limits, immediate family means parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, and adopted or foster children living in the driver's household. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A08
GDL step three, the full under-21 license at 18, requires a valid intermediate license, no alcohol-related offenses or traffic convictions in the last 12 months, and passing the vision and road sign tests. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A08
A new resident can transfer an out-of-state license that is valid or expired no more than 184 days, and a first-time applicant brings the Driver Examination Record (Form 100) showing the tests were passed. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0019]

Misconceptions: the Highway Patrol exam record never replaces the permit or license you must carry; renewal is your job even without a reminder; a suspended non-commercial driver may still renew, but a revoked one usually may not; the night-driving limit applies when driving alone, not when a licensed adult of the right age is along.
Mnemonics: the GDL ladder is permit, then intermediate, then full; for intermediate passengers think one, then three for young non-family riders.
Glossary: endorsement means an added privilege such as school bus or motorcycle; GDL means the Graduated Driver License law for first-time drivers under eighteen; immediate family means the household relatives listed for the passenger limits; DHH means the deaf or hard of hearing notation; first-person consent registry means your own donor decision is final without family approval.
Dynamic facts: renewal fees in reminder letters, office contact numbers and the donor and veteran websites can change and must be refreshed from the Department of Revenue website.
